spec.title: The overlay lands where the tracker sees things
spec.input: the worker’s correspondences each localized frame, projected through the renderer’s own projectWorld
spec.expected: the map’s positions projected through the world pose land on the tracker’s pixels
spec.failureCondition: a renderer that draws through a different projection from the one the pose was solved in

testResults.reason: what the renderer draws at a world point is where the camera sees it

spec.title: Draws only what the world holds
spec.input: every frame’s draw report against the world view and game state it was drawn from
spec.expected: no surface the world does not hold; no ring without a stage; nothing drawn without a pose
spec.failureCondition: fixed geometry on screen (Rule 002), or a goal drawn with no stage behind it

testResults.reason: every drawn object traces to the world or the stage generated from it

spec.title: The overlay box is the video box
spec.input: the canvas and video rectangles as laid out, read from the DOM
spec.expected: the same aspect ratio, so a processing pixel maps to the canvas by one uniform scale
spec.failureCondition: a canvas stretched differently from the video it overlays

testResults.reason: the overlay is laid exactly over the video

spec.title: The screen says what the engine says
spec.input: the HUD’s tracking label, read from the DOM each tick, against the world’s tracking state
spec.expected: TRACKING GOOD only when tracking is GOOD; LOST shown when it is lost
spec.failureCondition: TRACKING GOOD on screen while the engine is lost (Rule 002)

testResults.reason: the tracking label never claimed more than the engine had

spec.title: Drawing cost and rate
spec.input: time per overlay draw and the interval between display frames
spec.expected: cheap enough to keep the overlay near the display rate (§10: rendering as close to 60 fps as possible)
spec.passCriteria: median draw <= 6 ms; median frame interval <= 34 ms

controller.note: Every decision carries the median worker latency and the budget it was compared against. The controller reads no clock of its own — only the timestamps on the samples it is given (§59).

segmentLog.note: The timeline is cut wherever load injection was switched on or off. FRAME-001 reads the longest unstressed segment; stressed segments are measured and reported but never counted toward continuity.

crossCheckDetail.note: Each pair is one video frame measured twice: on the main thread with an independent 64x48 readback, and in the worker on the pixels the pipeline actually delivered. The readback costs what §H.1 measured, which is why it runs at 1 Hz and is excluded from the pipeline UI cost in FRAME-005.

pipeline.note: Frames declined by rate pacing (pacedOut) are the scheduler working as designed and are not drops. Frames declined because the worker was busy (backpressured) are deliberate too. Only `lost` counts frames that were handed over and never came back, and only that is held against FRAME-001.
